about: Open-source MCP servers Coordn8 registers for the host (Claude Code, user scope) and the sign-in-only tools it only OFFERS. Every server below was checked against its own registry metadata (npm registry JSON / PyPI JSON) and source repository LICENSE on the date above; the version is pinned to the one checked so a later licence change upstream cannot slip in unreviewed. Policy: no entry may be, or proxy, a hosted non-Anthropic AI model, hosted search, hosted web reader or hosted docs-AI service. Installed by scripts/mcp/install_mcp.py; this file is a menu, not a fence - a user may add their own servers alongside.

servers.name: Browser automation (Playwright MCP)
servers.licence_evidence: npm registry 'license' field for 0.0.83 = Apache-2.0; repository LICENSE file = Apache License 2.0
servers.purpose: Open the built page in a real browser, click through it and take screenshots, so the page and frame reviews look at the rendered artefact rather than its source.
servers.notes: Local browser only; no account, no hosted service. --headless avoids popping windows during a build; --isolated keeps the profile in memory so parallel sessions do not collide.

servers.name: Web fetch to Markdown (MCP fetch server)
servers.licence_evidence: PyPI 2026.10.19: license=MIT, classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License'; the source monorepo LICENSE states a transition from MIT to Apache-2.0 (both OSI-approved)
servers.purpose: Read current public documentation (release notes, library docs, the Claude Code docs index) straight from the publisher's page and turn it into Markdown on this machine, so 'as of <date>' facts come from the primary source with no hosted reader in between.
servers.notes: Runs locally under uvx; fetches the URL itself (honours robots.txt, refuses private addresses by default). No model, no hosted summariser.

servers.name: Filesystem (MCP filesystem server)
servers.licence_evidence: npm 'license' for 2.0.0 = 'SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE'; the repository LICENSE says new code is Apache-2.0 and contributions not yet relicensed remain MIT (both OSI-approved)
servers.purpose: Scoped read/write of the project folder for hosts and agent roles that have no native file tools, limited to the project the session runs in.
servers.notes: The allowed directory is the project root: Claude Code sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in a spawned server's environment and expands ${VAR:-default} in user-scope args. Version 2.0.0 declares node >= 24; the installer skips it with that reason on an older node.

servers.name: Blender bridge (headless, local Blender only)
servers.licence_evidence: npm 'license' for 0.1.6 = MIT (the Node server); the Python scripts it runs inside Blender sit under gpl/ with SPDX GPL-2.0-or-later headers and gpl/LICENSE.GPL; repository LICENSE = MIT
servers.purpose: Drive the Blender already installed on this machine in background mode: inspect a 3-D file, convert it to GLB for a page or scene, or run a bpy script that renders a still for a video scene.
servers.notes: Checked: zero runtime dependencies and no network calls in the published code; it never downloads or installs Blender. Registered only when Blender is present (requires_app).

signin_offers.name: claude.ai connectors (design, 3-D and image tools you choose)
signin_offers.why: Connectors you add at claude.ai appear in Claude Code automatically, so a stage can use a design, 3-D or image tool you already have an account for.
steps: Open https://claude.ai/customize/connectors (browse reviewed connectors at https://claude.ai/directory) and add the tool you want.
Complete that tool's sign-in at claude.ai.
In Claude Code run /mcp - connectors from claude.ai are listed with a claude.ai marker.
signin_offers.limits: Only works when Claude Code is signed in with a claude.ai subscription (not an API key or a cloud provider). On Team and Enterprise plans only admins can add connectors. Coordn8 policy: choose only tools that do not run a non-Anthropic AI model on your content.

signin_offers.name: Figma (design files, account sign-in)
signin_offers.why: Lets a design stage read frames, components and variables from your own Figma files instead of re-deriving them from screenshots.
signin_offers.command: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
steps: Run: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
Start a new Claude Code session, run /mcp, select figma, choose Authenticate and allow access in the browser.
signin_offers.limits: Needs a Figma account on a plan Figma lists for its MCP server. Coordn8 never runs this command or the sign-in for you.

signin_offers.name: Claude Design artboards (/design)
signin_offers.why: Drafts editable UI artboards from a brief, useful when a page layout needs several options to pick from.
steps: Sign in to Claude Code with a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise claude.ai account (Claude Code v2.1.234 or later).
In a session run: /design <what you want designed> and open the canvas link it prints.
signin_offers.limits: Research preview; available only where artifacts are available on your account. Nothing to install.
